Rh-Catalyzed oxidative homo-coupling cyclization
of 2,3-allenols to conjugated furylenones †
Xiaoyan Wu,
 Junjie Fan,
 Xin Huang and Shengming Ma
 *
An unexpected rhodium-catalyzed highly regio- and stereo-selective bimolecular nucleophilic oxyrhoda-
tion/insertion/1,4-Rh migration/β-H elimination reaction of 2,3-allenols a ﬀording (2,5-dihydrofuran-3-yl)
but-2(E)-en-1-one derivatives is reported. Optically active products may be prepared from optically active
2,3-allenols without obvious racemization. The synthetic potentials have been demonstrated.
Introduction
Cyclization involving two allenes has become a very important
approach for the synthesis of carbo- and hetero-cyclic
compounds.
1,2 In this area, Pd( II)-catalyzed cross-coupling
cyclization of allenes with a nucleophilic functionality in the
presence of 2,3-allenols or 2,3-allenyl acetates leading to highly
versatile 2,5-dihydrofuran derivatives
3–5 with a synthetically
useful conjugated 1,3-diene moiety 6 has been well established
(Scheme 1a). Besides the palladium catalysis, Hashmi and co-
workers also realized the cyclization of tertiary 2,3-allenols
under the catalysis of AuCl
3,a ﬀording a mixture of A-type
monocyclic products and B-type double cyclizative coupling
products together with other by-products (Scheme 1b). 7 In all
these cases, a β-O elimination process occurred to generate
conjugated dienes. Here, we wish to report a Rh( III)-catalyzed
regio- and stereo-selective bimolecular cyclization of 2,3-alle-
nols, in which one allenol cyclized to form the dihydrofuran
ring while the second molecule of allenol provided the conju-
gated enone unit, a ﬀording C-type derivatives with an exclusive
E-selectivity (Scheme 1c).
Results and discussion
Initially, the reaction conditions were optimized using 2,3-
allenol 1a (0.3 mmol) in the presence of [Cp*RhCl 2]2
(2.5 mol%) in methanol under an air atmosphere. The
expected products, such as the homo-coupling cyclization pro-
ducts A1 and B1 or the cycloisomerization product D1, were
not detected, and we merely observed the decomposition of
2,3-allenol 1a (Table 1, entry 1). When Cu(OAc) 2·H2O (2.0
equiv.) was added, the reaction a ﬀorded a new product, which
was later identified as enone ( E)-2a, in 15% NMR yield after
36 hours, unexpectedly (Table 1, entry 2). After a series of sol-
vents were screened, it was found that the reaction in CH 3CN
gave ( E)-2a in a slightly better yield of 20% with 23% recovery
of 1a (Table 1, entries 3 –8).
Considering the possible regeneration of the catalytically
active metal catalyst, the reaction was conducted under a pure
O
2 atmosphere and a higher yield of ( E)-2a was observed
(Table 2, entry 1). Increasing the loading of the Rh-catalyst to
4 mol% led to 38% yield of this product (Table 2, entry 2).
Further investigation of some mixed solvents showed that the
reaction in CH
3CN/MeOH (20/1) gave the best results (Table 2,
entries 3 –6). Changing the ratio of CH 3CN/MeOH all failed to
improve the yield (Table 2, entries 7 and 8). Further increasing

the loading of the Rh-catalyst and Cu(OAc) 2·H2O showed that
5 mol% of Rh-catalyst and 2.5 equiv. of Cu(OAc) 2·H2O gave the
best result (Table 2, entries 9 –13). However, the reaction was
rather sluggish when it was scaled up to 1 mmol (Table 2,
entry 14). Luckily, performing the reaction at a higher concen-
tration of 1a remarkably improved the rate and yield, a ﬀording
(E)-2a in 62% isolated yield at a concentration of 0.95 M
(Table 2, entries 15 –17). Thus, the conditions described in
entry 16 were chosen as the optimal conditions.
Halogen atoms (F, Cl, and Br) substituted on the para-,
ortho-o r meta-position of the phenyl groups could all be toler-
ated, leaving opportunity for further synthetic elaboration
(Table 3, entries 2 –6). The reaction of allenols bearing an elec-
tron-donating group-substituted phenyl group, 1g and 1h,
aﬀorded the products ( E)-2g and ( E)-2h in 57% and 44%
yields, respectively (Table 3, entries 7 and 8). In addition,
2-naphthyl substituted allenol 1i could also be transformed
into (E)-2i in 52% yield (Table 3, entry 9). Furthermore, hetero-
aryl groups such as 2-furyl and 2-thienyl substituted allenols
also led to the formation of ( E)-2j and ( E)-2k in decent yields
(Table 3, entries 10 and 11). Furthermore, the reaction of 1-cin-
namyl-2,3-butadienol ( E)-1l resulted in the formation of ( E,E,
E)-2l with four C vC bonds in 41% yield (Table 3, entry 12).
Primary alkyl group substituted 2,3-allenols could also react
smoothly to a ﬀord ( E)-2m–(E)-2r in 51% –64% yields (Table 3,
entries 13 –18). Primary alkyl groups containing functionalities
such as chlorine and a free hydroxyl group and secondary or
tertiary alkyl substituted allenols also worked well (Table 3,
entries 19 and 22). A gram-scale reaction could be easily rea-
lized (Table 3, entries 6 and 14).

The cross-coupling reaction of tertiary 2,3-allenol 1x and
secondary 2,3-allenol 1e aﬀorded the cross-cover product ( E)-
2xe in 49% yield together with the homo-coupling product ( E)-
2e in 17% yield (eqn (1)).
ð1Þ
The structure of the target molecule was unambiguously
determined by the X-ray single crystal di ﬀraction analysis of
(E)-2k (Fig. 1).
As we know, furan rings with chiral centres are very impor-
tant in pharmaceutical chemistry. 8 With this method, (2,5-
dihydrofuran-3-yl)but-2-en-1-one derivatives with a chiral
centre could be easily constructed from the readily available
optically active starting materials 9 without obvious loss of the
enantiomeric purity (Table 4).
To further explore the synthetic utility of this procedure, the
reaction was conducted on a 10 mmol scale, a ﬀording the
product ( S,E)-2f (>99% ee) in 50% yield under the standard
conditions (Scheme 2). ( S,E)-2f is synthetically versatile: the
reaction of Cp 2TiMe2 provided conjugated triene ( S,E)-3f in
68% yield.10 The two di ﬀerent C–Br bonds may be easily di ﬀer-
entiated: the Sonogashira coupling of the C –Br bond on the
electron-deficient phenyl ring with phenylacetylene gave ( S,E)-
4f in 78% yield exclusively. The Suzuki coupling of the same
C–Br bond with (4-methoxyphenyl)boronic acid a ﬀorded the
mono-coupling product ( S,E)-5f with a selectivity of 12/1 over
the double coupling product ( S,E)-6f. When 3 equiv. of
(4-methoxyphenyl)boronic acid were used, the double Suzuki
coupling product ( S,E)-6f was obtained in 65% yield
exclusively.
In order to gain insight into the mechanism of this trans-
formation, we conducted some control experiments
(Scheme 3). When 2-heptyl-2,3-butadienol 1w was applied
under standard conditions, the expected dimeric product ( E)-
2w was not observed. Instead, 14% yield of the cycloisomeriza-
tion product, 3-heptyl-2,5-dihydrofuran 7w, was isolated,
which may be formed via the protodemetalation of alkenylrho-
dium intermediate IN-1 (Scheme 3, eqn (1)). The unsuccessful
cross-coupling cyclization of allenol 1e with its corresponding
allenyl ketone 8e excludes the formation of in situ generated
allenyl ketone as the intermediate (Scheme 3, eqn (2)). When
the corresponding alcohol 9a was treated under standard con-
ditions, ( E)-2a was not formed with 87% recovery of 9a,
suggesting that ( E)-2a was not formed via oxidation of 9a
(Scheme 3, eqn (3)). The reaction of [D

product ( E)-2a without any deuterium incorporation
(Scheme 3, eqn (4)). Unexpectedly, the reaction of [D b]-1m
aﬀorded [D]-(E)-2m with a newly formed deuterated group with
99% of D incorporation (Scheme 3, eqn (5)).
Based on these experimental results, a mechanism was pro-
posed as shown in Scheme 4 using [D b]-1m as the substrate.
Firstly, 2,3-allenol [D b]-1m underwent a nucleophilic cyclic oxy-
rhodation to a ﬀord the 2,5-dihydrofuran-4-yl-rhodium inter-
mediate IN-1, which underwent an insertion reaction with the
second molecule of allenol to generate the stereodefined allylic
rhodium intermediate IN-2 stereoselectively by leaving the
dihydrofuran ring far away from the bulky hydroxyalkyl group
(IN-2 vs. IN-2′). This intermediate would form IN-3 via stereo-
defined 1,4-Rh( III) migration, 11,12 resulting in 1,4-D migration.
β-H elimination yielded the final product [D]-( E)-2m with the
generation of the Rh( III)H species. The Rh( III)H species under-
went a reductive elimination process to generate a Rh( I)
species, which was then oxidized to form the catalytically
active Rh(III) species by Cu(OAc) 2·H2O and O 2.12a–c
Conclusions
In summary, we have developed the first example of rhodium
(III)-catalyzed highly regio- and stereo-selective oxidative dimer-
ization of 2,3-allenols, providing an e ﬃcient approach for the
synthesis of (2,5-dihydrofuran-3-yl)but-2-en-1-one derivatives.
Such a reaction yields completely new products with a broad
scope of substrates and good functionality tolerance. The
stereoselectivity is determined by the steric e ﬀect between the
in situ formed furan ring and the bulky hydroxyalkyl group.
Optically active (2,5-dihydrofuran-3-yl)but-2-en-1-one deriva-
tives are e ﬃciently prepared from the readily available chiral
2,3-allenols. Further studies in this area are currently ongoing
in our laboratory.
